title: Projective morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. The morphism $f$ is *H-projective*, or *relatively projective*, if for some integer $n\geq0$ there is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ into projective space over $S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], such that $f=\pi\circ i$, where $\pi:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is the structural morphism. In this blueprint, $f$ is called *projective* if it is H-projective and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This is the H-projective convention of Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Definition Tag 01W8; that source uses the unqualified word *projective* for a possibly broader projective-bundle embedding. A scheme $X$ over a field $k$ is *projective over $k$* when $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is projective in the convention fixed here.
